## 1. What this is

Brand identity and creative work: [SELECT — logo and identity system / art
direction / motion and video / campaign assets / packaging].

Creative work differs from website work in one important way: **it is
subjective, and the contract has to account for that without becoming
unbounded.** The route-based structure below is how that's done.

Tick and complete what applies.

**Not included** — quoted separately

- Ongoing asset production _(see the retainer)_

## 3. Concepts and revisions

This clause is the one that keeps creative work finite.

### Concepts

The Studio presents **[3] initial routes**. Each is a genuine, distinct
direction — not one idea in three colours.

The Client selects **one route to develop**. Routes not selected are not
developed, and remain the Studio's property (clause 6).

### Revisions

**Two rounds on the selected route are included.**

- **Round 1:** refinement of the chosen direction — proportion, colour,
  weight, treatment.
- **Round 2:** final polish and file preparation.

Rules:
- One consolidated response per round, within **[5] working days**.
- Only **[NAMED APPROVER]** gives direction.
- **Rejecting all three initial routes** is not a revision. If it happens, the
  brief was wrong — the Studio will re-run discovery and present [2] further
  routes for **$[X]**. This is uncommon when the
  [branding questionnaire](../branding-questionnaire.md) has been completed
  properly, which is why it's mandatory before work starts.
- Switching to a different initial route after development has begun is a
  **new development cycle** at **$[X]**, because the work is not transferable.
- Additional rounds: **$[X]** each.

> Creative work can absorb infinite revision without converging. Three routes,
> one selection, two rounds is the structure that makes a fixed price
> possible — and it produces better work, because it forces a decision.

## 6. Intellectual property — replaces Common Clause 7

- **On final payment**, the Client receives full ownership of the **selected
  and delivered** identity and assets, worldwide, in perpetuity, for any
  purpose.
- **Unselected routes, concepts, sketches and explorations remain the
  Studio's property** and may be developed for other clients. The Client is
  purchasing the chosen work, not everything produced.
- Working files (layered source, motion project files) remain the Studio's
  unless purchased at **$[X]**. Delivered production files are the Client's.
- **Fonts and stock are licensed, not owned.** The Studio will specify what is
  required; the Client is responsible for holding correct licences for its own
  use. Font licences do not transfer.
- **Trademark is the Client's responsibility.** The Studio does not conduct
  clearance searches and gives no warranty that any mark is available or
  registrable. The Client should engage a trademark attorney before public
  use — this is normal and worth doing.

## 7. Portfolio rights — replaces Common Clause 8

The Studio may display the work, including unselected routes and process, in
its portfolio and marketing from the date the Client makes the identity
public, or **[6] months** after final delivery, whichever is earlier. Embargo
by written request.

## 8. Everything else

Clauses 1–6 and 9–14 of the [Common Clauses](common-clauses.md) apply.
